I use both fingers and a pick, depending on the song I'm trying to play. I play a lot of genres, so I've had to learn both. My background is in classical guitar, which means that I've been fingerpicking since the first time I picked up a guitar.

There's also a variety of 'attacks.' Attacks are the technique, speed, and force you use - as well as placement, when you cause the strings to vibrate. Depending on my fingernails, I may use a very specific portion of them. I may move my hand and pluck the string closer to the bridge for a sharper tone, or I may play closer to the neck, even past the sound hole - or even up on the neck itself, to get a very different tone.

Sometimes, I'm not even causing the vibrations with my right hand - but with the left by hammering on/off with my fret-hand.

There's many, many different ways to get sound from a guitar. There's even a technique (it's called golpe) where you use the body of the guitar as a percussion instrument. There's a whole host of slap techniques on the strings themselves.

Some, or all, of these can be combined to make music which you may or may not appreciate. Some will have greater sustain, some will have more warmth, some will accentuate specific parts of the sound spectrum, etc...

Yeah, guitar is my main instrument and it always will be. If I know the key, I can play a banjo along with people - without knowing the song. But, I'm really just regurgitating things I already know and, at most, changing them to a different key. If one were to listen long enough, and I were to play enough songs, they'd find I'm pretty much just repeating the same thing - over and over again with only the key having changed.

At the same time, give me a guitar and I'll be able to throw in a whole host of variations and even make things up on the fly. I'll toss in things that folks haven't heard before and combine them with things they'll never hear again. There's very little that I can't add something to - once I know the key and, maybe, where the key changes are. I can also watch a few bars and play along with people, just fine. If someone gets me started on the rhythm, I can keep that going and they can switch to lead and we can then bounce back and forth for as long as we want.

I can't do that on a banjo.
